question.whyItMatters: Quenby chases late payers every Monday morning.

text.text: Start here each morning: check what is due today, chase anything unpaid, then log your hours before you close the laptop.
A lead becomes a client when they say yes. Move the lead to Won and add them under Clients.
Create a project for each piece of work and give it a budget and dates.
Break the project into tasks. Mark them done as you go.
Log billable time as you work, with the rate you quoted.
Issue an invoice at each milestone and keep its status honest.
Overdue invoices are the ones past their due date and not yet paid. Change the status the day you notice.
Client: total billed, paid and balance owed.
Project: progress, hours against the estimate, and what is left to invoice.
Invoice: days late, from the due date.
Lead: days to the next follow-up.
Every Friday, ten minutes. The point is to leave the weekend without loose ends.
Clear the tasks waiting on clients with a gentle nudge.
Follow up on every lead whose date has passed.
Pick the three priorities for next week.

A Friday review turns the week into a list of things that are done and a short list of three priorities for Monday. Clients who are waiting on you hear from you before the weekend; clients who are late hear from you while the invoice is still fresh.
